clarification_questions.question: What is the physical state of the sample at the intended measurement point?
clarification_questions.decision_it_changes: Which method is recommended first (Liquid or solution: primary technique → NIR transmission or transflection probe; adds UV-Vis ATR probe to the shortlist; Powder or granules: unblocks Fluorescence fluorimetric probe; adds NIR surface at a distance to the shortlist; Paste, melt or slurry: primary method → MIR; unblocks Fluorescence fluorimetric probe)
clarification_questions.why_it_matters: The sample type decides which in-line techniques can be used at all.

clarification_questions.question: How far is the intended measurement point from where an analyzer could stand?
clarification_questions.decision_it_changes: Which method is recommended first (At the process, short cable: primary method → MIR; adds MIR ATR probe to the shortlist; In the next room: adds risk: a long fiber link; Far away, long cable run: adds risk: a long fiber link)
clarification_questions.why_it_matters: The link length limits which fibers and methods remain practical.

clarification_questions.question: If liquid is present at the measurement point, what does it look like?
clarification_questions.decision_it_changes: Which probe geometry or interface is used (Clear liquid: primary technique → NIR transmission or transflection probe; adds UV-Vis transmission or transflection probe to the shortlist; Turbid or cloudy: adds risk: a turbid or changing liquid (probe geometries to compare); Opaque, such as milky or dense: adds MIR ATR probe, UV-Vis ATR probe to the shortlist; drops NIR transmission or transflection probe, Raman probe from the shortlist)
clarification_questions.why_it_matters: The optical character decides between transmission, transflection and reflection or ATR geometries.

clarification_questions.question: Is a reference method available that provides comparison values for tumor boundary assessment?
clarification_questions.decision_it_changes: The acceptance criteria and the feasibility plan (Yes, a laboratory method: plan: calibrate against it and state its own error; No, none yet: plan: a reference measurement campaign comes first)
clarification_questions.why_it_matters: Models can only be as good as the reference values they are built on.

clarification_questions.question: Do you already have numerical acceptance criteria, such as required accuracy or a detection limit?
clarification_questions.decision_it_changes: The acceptance criteria and the feasibility plan (Yes, they are defined: plan: test against the agreed criteria; Not yet: plan: agree numerical criteria before the test)
clarification_questions.why_it_matters: Without them the experiment has no go or no-go criterion.

clarification_questions.question: Over what range must the target variable for tumor boundary assessment be followed?
clarification_questions.decision_it_changes: The acceptance criteria and the feasibility plan (Narrow, around a set point: plan: sample around the set point; Wide, from low to high: plan: sample the full range)
clarification_questions.why_it_matters: The range decides whether the sensitivity of a method can be enough.
